source: P01.270; Architect task and answered 2026-11-12T14:55:54Z; P01.266 F01-F07/F09 and class-2 navigation
removed:
A closed list. The text of `error` is for people and is not normative; the code, `kind` and the fields are.

- `key_rules`: a key not by the rules of N1 (empty, starting with `/`, with a segment `..`, longer than the limit) — the target key; for a guard row — a non-empty key not by the rules (an empty guard key is `badrequest`: out of the form of `guard`); the bytes of a read `key` after decoding are not UTF-8; a lone surrogate in `key` or `guard.key` (N2.1). Caller action: nothing: a code error.
- `body_form`: the body is not a JSON object or not JSON by N2.1 (a repeated field name, `NaN`, `Infinity`, a BOM, not UTF-8, deeper than the limit); `key` or `prefix` repeated in the query; the request does not parse as HTTP (N2.1); `op` is not `put`, `delete`, `batch` or `floor` (`floor` — P/01.3 N2); a lone surrogate in `items`; `key` of a command, `guard.key` or the read parameter `key` is absent or not a string; `items` is not an object of strings for `put`; `cas`, `guard`, `id`, `not_after` or `not_before` out of form (N1); `id` already belongs to another write; a batch out of the form of N1: `writes` absent, empty, not an array or longer than `BATCH_WRITES`, `guards` not an array or longer than `BATCH_GUARDS`, an element not in its closed form, a key twice in `writes` or in `guards`, a guard on a key from `writes`. Caller action: nothing: a code error.
- `no_route`: no route, or no such method on it (N2.1). Caller action: nothing.
- `identity`: the identity is not admitted by P/01.2 N3 «check» (list included): a role header on a role socket, an untrusted forwarding or a forbidden forwarded admin; `op: floor` not on the admin socket (P/01.3 N4). Caller action: fix the identity/trust; the absence of read by itself does not forbid list.
- `rights`: no rights (read, write, delete, guard read). Caller action: nothing: a deployment error or a foreign process (P/01.2 N4, rows «… without permission»).
- `cas_mismatch`: the version of the row is not the one in `cas`. Caller action: re-read, apply your own on top, repeat.
- `expired`: the admission time is later than `not_after` (N3 «Admission time»). Caller action: do not repeat with the same write: the deadline of the write has passed; a new one is decided by the caller by its own norm (an order — [P/03.6](../../03-worker/spec/03.6-worker.norms.md)).
- `early`: the admission time is not later than `not_before`. Caller action: do not repeat with the same write; a new write — at the next step (deleting a row with `made` — [P/04](../../04-controller/spec/04-controller.norms.md), P/03.6).
- `guard_mismatch`: the guard row is not at the version (for a batch — the first in the order of `guards`). Caller action: do not repeat: re-read the slot and check ownership anew ([P/03.2 N3 «write_under_slot»](../../03-worker/spec/03.2-worker.norms.md); the worker — [P/03.4 N4](../../03-worker/spec/03.4-worker.norms.md) «write under slot: `412 guard`»).
- `weight`: the row is heavier than the ceiling (for a batch — the first in the order of `writes`, nothing written). Caller action: nothing: what makes the row heavy goes into an object: a field `type: blob`, the bytes by the door `PUT /<rows>/<id>/<blob_field>` (P/06.1 N1.5, N2).
- `body_limit`: the body is larger than the read limit of N2; the store operation is not called. Caller action: shrink the body; compare its size with the body limit exactly.
- `no_leader_wait`, `lock_wait`, `connection_limit_doors`: no leader was found within the wait time, or the wait time of the local lock expired (item 1 of «Implementation decides»), or there are more connections than the declared limit of the door (`-max-conns` N1.3, a row of N4); the operation is **not done** — for a write, a read and a listing. Caller action: repeat at the next step of the cycle (with `Retry-After` — not before the deadline); hold what you hold.
- `floor_not_higher`: the service `op: floor` on the admin socket (only P/01.3 N2): the new value is not larger than the current one. Caller action: nothing: the lower bound of epochs is already not lower (P/01.3 N1.3).
- `ambiguous_leader`: the write reached the leader, the outcome is **unknown**. Caller action: repeat only with the same `id`; whoever cares — read first.
- `ambiguous_medium`: a medium error before the row is published, and the implementation cannot prove that the write will not apply after a restart (item 7 of «Implementation decides»); if it can — `unavailable`. Caller action: repeat only with the same `id`.
- `ambiguous_barrier`: the durability barrier (item 3 of «Implementation decides») refused when the bytes of the write were already on the medium: the row is published (it will come back after a restart), the outcome for the caller is **unknown** — on one box too. Caller action: repeat only with the same `id`: the replay completes the barriers and answers with the first answer (`again: true`), it hands out no new version; the barrier refused again — `ambiguous` again.
- `input_timeout`: an input phase expires after a correct supported request line and before execution (N2.1). Caller action: correct the pacing or declared input envelope; no applied id or business effect is inferred.
- `version_lost`: a read of a key or a listing that touches it, when the version of its row is lost (N2, R212, R384): damage to the store, not to the row; the log names the key. Caller action: repeat at the next step; the operator repairs the store.

## N5 Acceptance

Scenarios — [`../acceptance/1/scenarios.tsv`](../acceptance/1/scenarios.tsv) (judge-only: the scenario table of the
chapter; the readiness checklist below names the requirements each scenario checks), run through the door of N2 of any implementation by a role with full rights on the prefix `acc/`; the format is in `README.md` next to them. The path to the door (a unix socket or a stand with the same door) is a parameter of the runner, not a norm of the lesson. The log of AI corrections is `corrections-1.tsv` (judge-only: a historical correction record) of the lesson.

For this acceptance the runner prepares a door with the body limit **1048576 bytes (1 MiB)** and a store with the row
ceiling **524288 bytes (512 KiB)**. These are fixed parameters of the stand, not a universal body limit of all
implementations. The runner MUST check them by behaviour on a trial instance before the scenarios: a body exactly at the
limit reaches JSON parsing, one byte more — `413` with the body limit in `limit`; a weight of `items` exactly at the ceiling
is written, one byte more — `413` with the row ceiling. How to obtain an isolated instance with these parameters, the
implementation names in its description (item 10 of «Implementation decides»). If the parameters are not provided or the
check does not agree, the run is not performed and does not count as green.
Scenario 15 checks the weight of `items` after the body is parsed, scenario 22 — a refusal before the body is parsed by N2
(judge-only: sc. 15, sc. 22) — they check P/01.1-R073 and P/01.1-R036.
The comparison of the optional `size` in the second case is set in the acceptance README.

Detailed case descriptions and their expected outcomes are recorded in [N5 coverage](01.1-store.n5.cases.md) (judge-only: the N5 cases of the chapter). Governing rules and the public acceptance scope remain in this chapter.

An implementation whose store opens in the process without a door (files, memory) SHOULD (not MUST: acceptance norms the behaviour of the door, the internal API is the implementation's choice, item «Implementation decides») run the same scenarios
also through its API, mapping refusals to the codes of N4: so the order «guard before CAS» and the forms are checked in all its stores,
not only behind the door.

Unparseable HTTP (N2.1) is not expressible in TSV: the probe of the acceptance README checks it on raw bytes.

The equality boundary and both fractional sides, and non-decrease on one node at a clock move backwards and a reopen, are checked by the [seams](../acceptance/1/seams.tsv)
`s2-admission-equal`, `s3-admission-monotone`, `s5-reopen-id-admission` and `s9-reopen-refused-admission` (judge-only:
these seams of `seams.tsv`) — they check P/01.1-R070, P/01.1-R079, P/01.1-R080, P/01.1-R088, P/01.1-R264, P/01.1-R265, P/01.1-R270, P/01.1-R271, P/01.1-R277, P/01.1-R350, P/01.1-R351, P/01.1-R352, P/01.1-R392 and P/01.1-R393. Non-decrease at a leader change, continuation from a snapshot, a replay after `not_after` before the first copy is applied, and `admission_ahead` stay checked by reading:
the door does not move the leader's clock and does not hold a record between admission and application. They are debts of the [probe debt table](production-acceptance.md#probe-debt).

A power cut in the middle of a batch is checked by reading item 3 of «Implementation decides» and the code: the stand does not cut power; a restart after
a batch and a replay — (judge-only: sc. 30 of chapter 1.3) checks P/01.1-R135, P/01.1-R289 and P/01.1-R398, one log record in a group and forwarding by a door
without a vote — (judge-only: sc. 31 of chapter 1.3) checks P/01.1-R135 and P/01.1-R291. A body refusal of a batch over the limit is the
common body refusal before JSON parsing ((judge-only: sc. 22) checks P/01.1-R036). The row-count limit of the role
`console` — (judge-only: sc. 16 of chapter 1.2) checks P/01.1-R315.

## Implementation decides

Each implementation names in its description:
1. **the indivisibility mechanism** on one box (a file lock, a mutex) and in a group (a consensus log, in Go over the library of [the Raft library rule](../../common/versions/README.md#raft-library-and-implementation-boundary); a batch is one log record) and the lock wait time — what the caller gets when it expires (as `unavailable`);
2. **how a version is handed out**: a counter in a file, a log index plus the group base — as long as it does not repeat; which number it starts from;
3. **the disk layout** and **the durability barriers**. The order of one write: bytes to the medium, a barrier, publication and the answer; a delete survives a power loss. If the barrier refused when the bytes are already on the medium, the row is published and the answer is `ambiguous` (N4); a replay with the same `id` repeats the barrier. The barriers are not turned off: there is no environment variable and no flag for it, the flag set is closed ([daemon-flags.tsv](../forms/daemon-flags.tsv); P/01.3 N1.3 `durability`). **A batch:** how it becomes visible as a whole and after a power loss stays whole or does not appear at all (N3 «write batch», «Atomicity») — an intent log with a barrier before the rows are published, or another way; a lock is not enough: a lock does not survive power, and the rows of different files reach the medium separately;
4. **how a file-based implementation stores every admissible full key** within the file-system name limits;
5. **how a store that can read its row only partially** (a damaged file) reports it: the answer form is a norm (N2 `Row.unreadable`, P/01.1-17); here — how the implementation detects the damage and what it logs, and how it stores the version of the row so that damage to the body does not lose it (the loss of the version — 503, N2);
6. **the replay storage**: its bounded RAM cache, durable index, the retention minimum of N3 and the finite eligible-record collection budget under the qualified workload; the teaching non-durable mode is named separately;
7. **how the door tells «not added to the log» from «unknown»**; the leader wait time before `unavailable` follows the effective `-leader-wait` interval from the loss of the leader, by P/01.3 N1.3; its default is owned only by [daemon-flags.tsv](../forms/daemon-flags.tsv).
8. **the read limit of the HTTP body** of a store in the process without a daemon; for the daemon it is set by the flag `-max-body` (the source of defaults is [daemon-flags.tsv](../forms/daemon-flags.tsv)) separately from the row ceiling `-max-value`; the value and meaning of `limit` — by N2, the acceptance parameters — by N5.
9. **the request parsing limits**: the length of the HTTP request line (in bytes, without the final CRLF); exceeding it is `400 badrequest` by N2.1; the length of a chunk-size line of chunked with extensions (without CRLF) — exceeding it is a framing error: `400 badrequest` and the connection closed; the drain volume and time after an early refusal (N2.1). The header limit (`HEADER_BYTES`) and the JSON depth (`JSON_DEPTH`) are norms of N2.1, not a choice; The finite positive monotonic idle/header/body/drain budgets and their exact start events are N2.1; the implementation declares their values and any separate inactivity timer before qualification. Measurement allowance is separate and does not enlarge a protocol deadline.
10. **how the runner obtains an isolated instance** with the acceptance parameters of N5: the start command with substitutions by the section «Stand» of the acceptance README of this lesson — it is common to the acceptance of M10; the lesson does not norm an internal API;
11. **how a listing takes its list** (a copy under the lock, a version snapshot); the guarantee of the «Races» of N3 is kept.

removed: Procedures are numbered algorithms («1. Let … 2. If …, return …»): steps\nrun in order, and «return» ends the procedure.
- An unreadable record is one that is not JSON, not an object, not in the record form of the lesson, or not in its place.
- The exception is a record without which the answer is false; the lesson names it explicitly (for example, a marker that\n  decides the outcome).
- A lesson that assembles such an answer names the skip counter and gives a step: one spoiled record — 200 and the counter.
- A field whose form is `float` in [P/06.1](../../06-console/spec/06.1-console.norms.md) N1.2 (table stamps, `sweep.at`\n  there) is also written by the writer in the shortest notation.
- The value of a time notation is finite in binary64: overflow is also out of form.
- The time fields of each lesson are listed at the start of its N1 («Time»). In the data catalogue this is the\n  common type «time».

At a common move of the clocks the consequences follow their own conditions: admission time does not decrease (R264); `expired` depends on `not_after` (R270); `admission_ahead` appears when the current clock of the leader is behind the saved admission time (R348; N3 «Admission time», P/01.3 N1.3 `admission`). No new route is added for it.
- owns: no rows — the lesson sets the store operations over any rows; the rows of the store daemon are chapter 1.3;

- reads: `/etc/w2c/configstore-rights.json` (the rights of roles to every operation, P/01.2 N1.2), `/etc/w2c/tls/ca.pem`, `/etc/w2c/tls/<role>/server.pem`, `/etc/w2c/tls/<role>/server.key`, `/etc/w2c/tls/revoked`, `/etc/w2c/tls/crl.pem` (a door off the loopback, P/01.3 N1.6).
The store is a map key → row; it has no other entities.
A key MUST NOT be empty.
A key MUST NOT start with `/`.
A key MUST NOT have a segment (between `/`) equal to `..`.
If a key breaks a key rule (R153–R156), then the store MUST answer `badkey`; the key is not repaired.
One spelling of a key is one place: keys are compared by UTF-8 bytes, without normalization — `a//b`, `a/./b`, `a/b/`\nand the NFC and NFD forms of one text are different keys.
The order of the fields of `items` has no meaning.
`items` MUST keep its weight (sum of byte lengths of every key and every value) at most the store's ceiling `ROW_CEILING`.
A version is never the same twice within one store.
One version per operation: a batch (N3 «write batch») hands out one version, and every row it writes gets it; «never the\nsame twice» counts operations, not rows.

«Never the same twice» is about versions handed out: a version a write or a delete hands out is not handed out again; a\nrow carried in by import or restore keeps the copy's version (P/01.3-R140) — not handed out by this store, it may equal one\nhanded out before the transfer (P/01.3 N1.3 import).
`""` names an absent row and is no version.
If `cas` is `""`, then the write MUST apply only while the row does not exist (creation; the first one wins).
If `cas` is a version, then the write MUST apply only while the version of the row is exactly this one.
The guard MUST be checked in the same operation as `cas`.
The rights to the guard row are the caller's read rights: `allowed(role, read, guard.key)` (P/01.2 N1.3 guard, N3\n«check»).
`not_after` and `not_before` MUST be finite and at least 0; finite is finite in binary64, like codec time (codec.tsv\n`time`): `1e400` is `badrequest`.
`not_after` and `not_before` are JSON numbers compared by value: the value and the comparison go by the binary64 value; the\nreplay fingerprint goes by R280.
If `not_after` or `not_before` is `null`, a string, a bool or a negative number, then the door MUST refuse with\n`badrequest`: it is out of form (as for `id`).
A log record with `not_before` MUST apply only if its admission time is strictly later than `not_before`; otherwise the answer is `early`\n(N4).
Both conditions MAY stand in one record.
A client SHOULD put `id` on every write (32 hex digits of randomness).
After an «unknown» answer only a replay with the same `id` is safe (N4; the worker — P/03.4-07: every write of it that\ncarries a value carries an id, after `ambiguous` — a replay with the same id).
The order of `writes` matters.
A key occurs in `writes` once.
`items` of an element of `writes` is required for put.
For put, the form of `items` of an element of `writes` is that of `row.items`; its ceiling is that of `row.items`, per row\n(R200).
`items` of an element of `writes` is not read for delete.
The order of `guards` matters.
A key occurs in `guards` once.
A key of `guards` does not occur in `writes`: the condition of a written row is its `cas`.
`guards` MUST have at most `BATCH_GUARDS` elements (except the roles `console` and `domain`, R020, R315).
An element of `guards` is closed — exactly the fields `key`, `index`.
`BATCH_GUARDS` is at least `FOLDERS_DEPTH_MAX + 1` (P/06.8 N1.3).
`KEY_BYTES`, `BATCH_WRITES` and `BATCH_GUARDS` are the named limits in [runtime-constants.tsv](../forms/runtime-constants.tsv).
The body weight limit still applies to the role `domain`.
Guards have no weight.
The sum of the weights of the rows of `writes` is not compared with the ceiling: the body limit of N2 holds it.\n\n<!-- removed: P/01.1-R021 by ADR-0133 -->
The limit of a single component is not the limit of the resulting path: for example, a unit name of 1000 bytes gives\n`testsub/counters/…` of 1017 bytes.
There is no common limit of 200 bytes for platform keys.

The admissible grammar of components does not guarantee that the full key fits the chosen store; the refusal is\n`400 badkey` by N4, with no change to the row. The application of this refusal by the unit door is\n[P/06.1](../../06-console/spec/06.1-console.norms.md) N3–N4, by the worker — [P/03.2](../../03-worker/spec/03.2-worker.norms.md).
`error` is required in a refusal, although acceptance usually does not compare its text.
A version in an answer has the form of N1, not of an arbitrary string.
A batch `conflict` also carries `key` — the row whose `cas` differed; a single write has no `key`.
The size `size > limit`, the actual bytes and the order of `keys` are checked separately: one JSON Schema does not prove\nthese relations.
A guard compares with the version of a damaged row.
A write and a delete with `cas` on the version of a damaged row pass.
The version of a row is stored so that damage to the body does not lose it (how — item 5 of «Implementation decides»).
A listing that touches a key whose version is lost is 503 `unavailable` (`version_lost`, N4) with a log entry until\nrepaired, not a skip.

If the current version needed by a put, delete, batch or guard is lost, the operation MUST return 503 `unavailable` (`version_lost`) without its business effect, issuing a version or occupying its `id`. This includes an unconditional put or delete. The check runs when the procedure reads that version, after replay and deadlines; admission metadata follows P/01.1-R070 independently.
The byte limit of N1 is checked separately after encoding in UTF-8.
- If `guard.key` is empty, then the door MUST refuse with `badrequest`.
- `guard: null` is out of form, `badrequest`.
- `guards: null` is out of form, `badrequest`.
Against the body limit the bytes of the HTTP body are counted, without headers, before JSON parsing.

The framing of N2.1 and this limit are the first step of every request of the doors of the store, whatever its method and\nroute: a body larger than the limit is `413 toolarge` (`body_limit`) before the route, the identity and the form of the\nbody.
A body of `GET` within the limit is read and discarded; it is not data of the operation.
- While the body is not larger than the limit, it passes to JSON parsing and the checks of N3.
- If the body exceeds the limit, then the door MUST refuse with `413 toolarge` before calling the store operation: the row,\n  the version and the `id` memory do not change.
- `limit` in this refusal is the body limit.
- `limit` in the refusal for an exceeded row weight is the row ceiling.
- If the full size of the body is known, the body refusal MAY contain `size` with this size in bytes; if it is unknown,\n  `size` is absent.
- `key` is not returned in a body refusal: the JSON has not been parsed yet.
- The acceptance settings are given in N5; the way to set the limit is the implementation's choice.
Extra top-level fields of the command `POST /v1/write` are not part of the replay fingerprint.
The bytes of extra fields count towards the total size of the HTTP body.
The rule of extra fields does not extend to the content of `guard`: its form is closed by N1; `items` is checked by N1 for\nput and not read for delete by N3.
The list of codes and kinds is closed: a new one only by an edit of this lesson.
- In a name and a value of the query `+` is a space.
- In a name and a value of the query `%XX` is a byte; a `%` not followed by two hex digits stays as written.
- Empty pairs of the query (`&&`) are skipped.
- A parameter without `=` has the value `""`: `?key` gives an empty key, `badkey` (N1).

- After the table [`read-checks.tsv`](../forms/read-checks.tsv) of a read and a listing come the identity and the rights\n  of P/01.2 N3 «check» by the table [`rights-checks.tsv`](../forms/rights-checks.tsv).
- An absent `prefix` is an empty prefix, all rows.
- An absent `key` of a read is `400 badrequest` (R030).
- `prefix` is bytes after decoding, UTF-8 is not required (N3 «list»).
- Other query parameters of a read and a listing are not read.
- A query of `POST /v1/write` is not read.
- `Content-Type` is not checked.
- `NaN` and `Infinity` in the body of `POST /v1/write` — `400 badrequest`.
- A BOM before the body of `POST /v1/write` (§8.1) — `400 badrequest`.
- Non-UTF-8 bytes in the body of `POST /v1/write` (§8.1) — `400 badrequest`.
- A lone surrogate (`\\ud800`) in `key` or `guard.key`, or for a batch in the `key` of an element of `writes` or `guards` —\n  `400 badkey`: the string cannot be encoded in UTF-8 nor measured by N1.
- A lone surrogate in a name or value of `items` — `400 badrequest`.
- A lone surrogate in extra fields is not read.
- Numbers and strings of extra fields are not read at any length.

- The nesting depth is one number for all implementations: `JSON_DEPTH` ([runtime-constants.tsv](../forms/runtime-constants.tsv)) nested objects and arrays from the root, the root object counts 1, in any field,\n  extra ones too; depth `JSON_DEPTH + 1` — `400 badrequest`.
- The early refusal MUST carry `Connection: close`.
- The door MUST NOT parse or execute the rejected body whose bytes it discards.
- Discard stops earlier at the declared raw-byte limit.
- Discard stops earlier at the absolute monotonic drain deadline.
- A chunked sender need not send a terminal chunk for discard to finish.
- The drain volume and time are declared in item 9 of «Implementation decides».
- Incoming bytes do not extend the drain interval.
- A fault response is not added after this refusal.
- `HEAD` is also `404`, without a body (RFC 9110 §9.3.2).
- **Request line and headers.** A line ends only with CRLF: a lone LF or CR — `400 badrequest`.
- Empty lines before the request line — `400 badrequest` (they are not skipped).
- The request target is only the bytes 0x21–0x7E without `#`; any other byte (a raw `\\x00` included) — `400 badrequest`.
- `%00` in the request target is three admissible bytes: the query key after percent-decoding contains U+0000 and is\n  admissible by N1; the path is compared byte for byte by R051.
- There is no separate limit on the number of header lines.
- Several `Content-Length` with different values — `400` and the connection closed.
- A chunk size of chunked is HEXDIG only (`0x5` — `400`).
- A `Transfer-Encoding` other than exactly `chunked` — `400` (`gzip, chunked` and two TE lines too).
- A length number larger than the implementation can represent — `413 toolarge`: it is certainly larger than the body\n  limit, no `size`.
- After any framing error the door MUST close the connection.
- The request line, the headers and the body framing are parsed by [RFC 9112](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112):\n  obs-fold is a parsing violation (§5.2).
- A space before the colon of a header is a parsing violation (§5.1).
- With `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` together the body is read as chunked (§6.3).

- A request that does not parse as HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/1.0 (no version, a wrong request line or header, a request line or\n  headers longer than the limit of item 9) is `400 {kind: badrequest}` with a `Fault` body. The codes 414, 431, 501, 505\n  and default server pages are not in the closed list.
- These intervals are measured by monotonic time.
- A slow trickle MUST NOT extend an absolute deadline.
- Any additional inactivity interval is declared separately.
- At an input timeout a response that has already started gets no second fault.
- This timeout rule does not replace R244: EOF or a truncated body still receives no answer, is not executed and does not occupy an id.
- The phase budgets describe P/01 input, not a common deadline for forwarding, pass or stream responses owned by other lessons.

- Before the table a request of `POST /v1/write` passes, in this order: the frame (the framing of R054 and the body limit,
  R034 — `413 toolarge`), the route (`404`), the identity of P/01.2 N3 «check» steps 1–2 (a role header on a role socket,
  the trust of a forwarding — `403`), the JSON form of this section (`400`); `403` by rights is a row of the table. A body
  larger than the limit with a role header is therefore `413`.

- The native output of the vector package `01-store/write-checks` is one JSON object: `{"n": 0}` when no row is violated, otherwise `{"n": <the first violated row>, "code": <its code>, "kind": "<its kind>"}`. The column `fault` is not in this output: it belongs to the door.

- The envelope of the vector package `01-store/write-checks`, package, table, case and cells, is its row of the form [`probe-tables.tsv`](../../common/vectors/probe-tables.tsv), described in the [P/01 write-checks transport](../../common/vectors/wire.md#p01-write-checks-transport).
- The profile of `01-store` declares the `vectors` entry `01-store/write-checks`.
A batch is, moreover, indivisible against a power loss: «write batch», «Atomicity».
2. If the caller has no read right, return `forbidden` (P/01.2 N3 «check»: `allowed(role, read, key)`).
3. If the row `key` does not exist, return (null, "").
4. If the row exists but is not readable (N2), return (null, index, `unreadable: true`).
5. Return (a copy of items, index).
1. For each row whose key starts with prefix (byte comparison), output its index.
Identity is checked before the operation by P/01.2 N3 «check»: a substituted role or an untrusted forwarding gives 403 forbidden.

For a listing the rows of [`read-checks.tsv`](../forms/read-checks.tsv) (413, 404, 400 of the query) MUST come before the check of identity ([`rights-checks.tsv`](../forms/rights-checks.tsv)), and both before the procedure: a repeated `prefix` with a substituted role gives 400.
The prefix check gives no 400 except for a repeated parameter (N2.1).
A listing does not require read rights to values: it names names and versions, not content.
N2 of the door for a listing: 200; 400 of the parsing of N2.1 (a repeated `prefix`, R259); 403 of identity; 404 no route or not `GET`; 413 of the body limit (R217); 503.
A prefix SHOULD end with `/`: `testsub/count` would match both `testsub/counters/…` and `testsub/countdown`.
```\nadmitted := max(the leader's clock when the record is admitted to the log, the admission time of the previous log record)\n```

When a record is **applied**, the conditions `not_after` and `not_before` MUST be checked against this stored time, not\nagainst the clock of the applying server: the outcome is one on all servers of the group and does not depend on when the\nrecord reached application.
The admission time MUST NOT decrease along the log: a new leader and a restarted daemon continue from the admission time\nof the last record of their log (including one that came by snapshot).
Such a store MUST store the admission time as durably as rows: under the same lock and the same durability barrier as the\nwrite (item 3 of «Implementation decides»).
The admission time is part of the store state and its snapshot (P/01.3 N1.3 `admission`).
The copy `copy` of P/01.3 does not carry the admission time: a group after `import` or `restore` starts from the clock of\nits leader.
A write answer does not return the admission time.
A leader clock that ran ahead raises the admission time, and writes with `not_after` get `expired` until the clock\ncatches up.
An admission time raised by a leader clock that ran ahead is visible by the flag `admission_ahead` (P/01.3 N2 `/v1/status`).
The previous admission value and both bounds use the same numeric domain as the converted clock reading (R304).

Storage, restoration and application MUST preserve the assigned binary64 numeric value. They MUST NOT additionally round it to integer seconds or milliseconds, or apply the row-writer notation limit of N0.
For an admission time A, `not_after` admits A <= bound and refuses A > bound, also on fractional boundaries (N1).
For an admission time A, `not_before` admits A > bound and refuses A <= bound, also on fractional boundaries (N1).
The admission time of such a replay must survive an ordinary close/reopen as the last admission metadata.
A subsequent rollback of the physical clock cannot undo the admission time of such a replay.
2. If the weight of items exceeds the ceiling, return `toolarge` (nothing written).
3. If the caller has no write right to key, return `forbidden` (P/01.2 N3 «check»: `allowed(role, write, key)`).
4. If guard is given and the caller has no read right to guard.key, return `forbidden`.
6. Let admitted be the admission time of this record (above, «Admission time»).

2. Otherwise return its answer with again=true; the rows, issued versions and applied-id entry do not change. The last admission time still advances with its durability by R271 and N3 «Admission time» (R070, R264, R265, R392), even when the answer comes from this memory.
9. If not_before is given and admitted ≤ not_before, return `early`; nothing is written.

11. If guard is given:\n    1. Let at be the version of the row guard.key ("" if absent); a lost version follows P/01.1-R402.\n    2. If at ≠ guard.index, return `guard` {key: guard.key, index: at}; nothing is written.
12. If cas is given and cas ≠ current, return `conflict` {index: current}; nothing is written.
14. Set the row key to (a copy of items, index).
16. Return index.
A replay of an applied write gets its answer also after `not_after`.
A replay that arrived after `not_after` while the first copy was not yet applied gets the answer of the first copy too:\nthe first one is applied first, the replay answers with its answer.
A refusal `expired` and `early`, like `conflict` and `guard`, makes no write and does not take the `id`.
Only `expired` remains the same refusal for the same deadline and nondecreasing admission time.
`early`, `conflict` and `guard` do not occupy the `id`: the same command and `id` are checked again against the current admission time and state and may succeed.

A guard refusal means a mismatch of the observed version and the absence of this write. The caller re-reads the condition and decides anew whether it has the right to repeat; a version mismatch by itself does not prove a loss of ownership.
A CAS refusal also requires a re-read before a new attempt.
The admission time so updated by R277 is persisted by the same rule as admission in the successful case (N3 Admission time).
An id mismatch keeps the first applied-id entry and its original answer, without replacing or freeing them.
Items are copied on output: the store does not share the memory of the returned items with the caller.
In the replay fingerprint `cas: null` equals the absence of `cas`.

Both `not_after` and `not_before` of the fingerprint are compared by their finite binary64 numeric values as in N1 (`10` and `10.0` are one), absence equals no number. Distinct JSON number spellings that round to the same binary64 value compare equally and have the same bound fingerprint; exact decimal-rational comparison and raw spelling are not the bound domain.
This numeric rule does not apply to versions: they remain exact strings, and `"0"` is not `""`.
- Two writers with one `cas` on one row: exactly one passes, the second gets `conflict` with the version of the first.
- Two creations with `cas: ""`: exactly one passes.
- After an «unknown» answer the caller does not distinguish these two cases of a replay and must not.
- A replay with the same `id` but other content (other `items`, `cas` or `guard`): refusal `badrequest`, nothing written — an identifier belongs to one write.
- A leader change between admission and application: the caller gets `ambiguous`; see above.

- A write with `not_after` and its replay with the same `id` after `not_after`: if the first one applied, the replay answers\n  with its answer (R272); if not, the replay applies as the first and gets `expired`.
2. If the caller has no delete right to key, return `forbidden` (P/01.2 N3 «check»: never N1.3, `allowed(role, delete, key)`).
3. If guard is given and the caller has no read right to guard.key, return `forbidden`.
5. Let admitted be the admission time of this record.
If they match, return the former answer with again=true.
If they do not match, return `badrequest`.
In either branch the business rows, issued versions and original applied-id entry stay unchanged; the newly admitted time is retained durably by R265, R271, R277, R392, also for a mismatch.
8. If not_before is given and admitted ≤ not_before, return `early`.
10. If guard is given, read the version of guard.key by P/01.1-R402; if it differs from guard.index, return `guard`.
11. If cas is given and cas ≠ current, return `conflict` {index: current}.
13. Let index be a new version (a delete spends a version).
15. Return index.
A delete spends a version so that a stale `cas` on a deleted and re-created row does not pass.
A delete of an absent row is done.
A replay of a done delete is the same delete.

With `cas ""` on an absent row a delete changes nothing (the row was absent and stays absent; the read version stays `""`), and a following write with `cas ""` passes — there is nothing to choose a winner from here.
2. For each put in the order of writes: if the weight of its items exceeds the ceiling, return `toolarge` {key, size, limit} of this row; nothing is written.

3. Rights in the order of writes: `allowed(role, write | delete, key)`; then in the order of guards: `allowed(role, read, key)`;\n   if one is missing, return `forbidden` for the whole batch (P/01.2 N3 «check»); nothing is written.
5. Let admitted be the admission time of this record (above, «Admission time»).

2. Otherwise return its answer with again=true; the rows, issued versions and applied-id entry do not change. The last admission time still advances with its durability by R271 and N3 «Admission time» (R070, R264, R265, R392), even when the answer comes from this memory.
8. If not_before is given and admitted ≤ not_before, return `early`; nothing is written.

10. For each write in the order of writes: let current be the version of the row key ("" if absent); a lost version follows P/01.1-R402, also without cas. If cas is given and cas ≠ current, return `conflict` {key, index: current}; nothing is written.
11. Let index be a new version, never handed out before by this store — one per batch.
14. Return index.
The order is normative: form → weight → rights → the `id` memory → deadlines → guards in\nlist order → `cas` in list order → application; the answer is the first violation.
A guard on a written key is a form refusal: the condition of such a row is its `cas`.
The admission time of a batch refused with `expired`, `early`, `guard` or `conflict` remains the last admission time, as\nfor a write.
A refusal names the row but not the value: `412 guard {key, index}`, `409 conflict {key, index}` — the version of this\nrow now.

The refused batch still updates the last admission time to this record's `admitted` (which may equal the previous time). Zero business-row changes, no occupied `id` and no issued version do not mean rolling back this admission metadata. This applies to each of the four named refusals after admission, not to a request rejected before admission.
An admitted batch returning `badrequest` for an id mismatch also retains its new last admission time. This does not apply to a request rejected before admission.
An admitted batch returning `badrequest` for an id mismatch has no business-row or issued-version effects; its original applied-id entry and answer remain unchanged (R278).
The admission time that a batch keeps by R285 or R286 has the same durability as admission of a successful batch.
A delete of an absent row in a batch is done.
The `id` memory is one for writes and batches, its lifetime — the section below, a batch counts as one write: an `id`\ntaken by a put is `badrequest` for a batch, and vice versa.
After a power loss at any point, a barrier refusal included, the whole batch or none of its rows is visible.
The `id` memory of a batch is durable together with it: a replay does not complete half a batch, because there is no half.

The `ambiguous` branch of N4 (a medium error, a barrier refusal, a leader change) applies to the whole batch: a replay\nwith the same `id` answers with the first answer or applies the batch as the first.
In a group a batch is one log record; the way of a box and of a store in the process is item 3 of «Implementation\ndecides».
**Races.**
- Two batches with a common row and one `cas`: exactly one passes, the second gets `conflict` with the version of the first; none of its rows is written.

- Two reads of two rows of a batch are two operations: the first may be before the batch, the second after. One operation sees the batch whole; the caller compares versions: the rows of one batch have one version.
- A replay with the same `id` together with the first application: as for a write, the first copy is applied first.
A forgotten replay is applied as a new write — hence `cas` on every write that matters.
The age in the condition of R141 runs from the first application; its clock basis is admission time (N3 «Admission time»), because admission time survives a restart; both lower conditions stay.
**Races.** A replay and a new write with the same `id` but other content at once: the earlier one is applied first, the second gets 400.
**Scope: production.** Checkpoint work of persistence is accounted separately and in the amortized total; a background thread does not hide it.
**Scope: production.** After this check import builds the state without repeatedly rewriting the already processed prefix. Indexed construction or sorting in O(N log N) is allowed.
**Scope: production.** Under this rule existing versions, the floor, transfer phases and durability barriers are preserved.

**Scope: production.** The implementation declares its cost model and the qualified workload/resources; input bytes and stored-row cardinality are measured separately. No universal numeric ceiling is supplied by this rule.

The OpenAPI fault schemas and the orders of checks ([`forms/write-checks.tsv`](../forms/write-checks.tsv), [`forms/read-checks.tsv`](../forms/read-checks.tsv)) stay their owning forms; the causes, priority and caller actions below refer to stable refusal names, without duplicating the outcome cells.
An unknown medium outcome stays `ambiguous`; rolling back RAM alone does not prove no effect after recovery.
After `ambiguous_barrier` a replay with the same `id` completes the required barriers and returns the first answer with `again`, without a new version.

After `ambiguous_barrier` another barrier failure of the replay remains `ambiguous`. A later, distinct write is judged by its own effect: if it is refused before any effect and the store proves it cannot apply after recovery, its outcome is `unavailable`, not `ambiguous` merely because the earlier write is unresolved. If its effect is unknown, it remains `ambiguous`; a successful write requires its durability barriers. This does not require freezing all later writes.

A refused connection (an overflowing `accept` queue; there is no separate 503) is on the client side too: `no_reply` of the store client contract. The column «What the caller does» is there too, section «Outcomes and what the client does».
